title: Clarify validation hierarchy and affordance contrast for mixed-density forms
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Mixed-density screens (a combination of compact and comfortable rows) currently show inconsistent validation signals, helper text placement, and focus affordance contrast. Engineers and PMs have reported regressions when switching density tokens — error toasts and inline errors sometimes compete with helper microcopy, and the focus ring is either too subtle in compact rows or too visually dominant in comfortable rows. This causes user confusion and accessibility gaps (screen reader verbosity, unclear error precedence) and increases support tickets for form-based workflows (billing, onboarding).

Goal: Define a clear validation hierarchy and concrete affordance contrast rules that work across density modes and component types (text fields, selects, toggles, textarea). Output should include updated Figma tokens/specs, CSS token mappings, accessibility guidance (SR announcements, error priority), and a small set of engineering acceptance tests (visual diff + axe/voiceover checks).

Scope: All text-based inputs, single-select, multi-select chips, toggles used in forms, and multi-line textarea components. Not in scope: data tables or charts with inline editors (handled in separate ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Design token mapping: clear contrast ratios (WCAG AA minimum) for focus, hover, error, and disabled states in both compact and comfortable density; tokens documented in Figma and a single JSON token export

Validation precedence doc: explicit rules for which message shows (error > warning > helper > success) including timing (on blur, on submit, live) and how multiple messages coexist in crowded helper rows
Microcopy guidelines: examples for short/long helper text truncation vs. expanding details link; consistent voice for required/optional and error messages
Accessible announcement spec: SR announcement phrasing and when to announce (on error, on success, on change of helper text); example ARIA attributes to apply
Component specs: updated padding, text-size, and focus outline thickness per density for text input, select, toggle, textarea; Figma components and tokens updated
Engineering checklist: visual regression snapshots for each density and state; axe/pa11y rules passing for forms using updated tokens
QA flows: small end-to-end script for billing form and user profile edit form demonstrating clear validation precedence
notes: Design exploration took place 2026-03-03; two alternatives considered: (A) single universal focus token with density-driven scale, (B) separate focus tokens for compact vs comfortable. Team consensus favors (B) because it preserves perceived click target in compact mode without increasing perceived noise in comfortable mode.

Trade-offs: stronger focus outlines in compact mode improve discoverability for keyboard users but increase visual weight for sighted users. We'll mitigate with token-based alpha adjustments and a subtle inset shadow option for comfortable rows.

Edge case: inline validation for multi-select chips — error should attach to the field label and not to each chip to avoid verbosity. Provide example markup for aria-describedby linking to a single error node.
Related research: moderated usability session (n=8) showed 3x fewer mis-submissions when inline errors are placed above the helper row rather than below it in compact layouts.
Design files: updated components will live in Figma page 'Forms / Density & Validation (DES-31901)'.

Engineering note: backend form errors often arrive as an array; map server errors to first-field-first policy by default, with an optional server-supplied priority field. We'll include example error-mapping code in the handoff.
Risks: changing token contrast may affect other surfaces; will run a cross-surface visual diff and coordinate with Tokens inventory owners before merge.
decisions: Use density-specific focus tokens rather than a single scaled token — chosen for clarity in compact layouts (Decision: Marco Liu, 2026-03-05).
Validation precedence will be error > warning > helper > success with 'error' visually taking precedence and announced immediately on blur/submit (Decision: Aisha Patel + UX Research, 2026-03-06).
Helper text collapse pattern: truncate to one line with 'More' link for long explanations in compact mode; comfortable mode shows up to two lines before collapse.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Marco Liu: Initial audit completed across main product pages (billing, signup, workspace settings). Found 18 instances where helper text overlapped with inline errors in compact density.
2026-03-04 - UX Research (Nila Rao): Usability sessions show clear preference for errors above helper text in compact mode; will attach raw transcripts in Confluence.
2026-03-08 - Design Review (Ethan Park): Approved token contrast targets for error and focus in comfortable mode; requested revised specs for high-contrast mode and dark theme.

2026-03-10 - Engineering (Priya Menon): Noted that current select component uses native browser focus ring in some browsers — we'll need a small polyfill/patch for consistent outline behavior across platforms.
2026-03-12 - Accessibility Lead (Josef Becker): Agreed on SR announcement phrasing; asked for explicit examples using aria-live polite for helpers and assertive for errors.
